comment: Every entry point under scripts/e2e/, in one of two lists, read by .github/workflows/e2e.yaml.
`hosted` is the set a GitHub-hosted runner can run: each row says what the job must give that
script, and `why_hosted` is a note on why a hosted runner can run it, read by no job. `elsewhere`
is every other script, each with the `needs` its own header states; e2e.yaml refuses one by
name with that text, and the refusal is a failed job. Both lists together must name every
scripts/e2e/*.sh of the tree, and e2e.yaml's select job fails when one is missing or extra.
`apt` is what the job installs for that script alone, `bun` whether it needs bun and this
repository's node_modules, `evidence_variable` the environment variable the script reads for
its evidence directory (empty where it takes none and keeps its work directory instead), and
`timeout_minutes` the job's limit, measured from the script's header with headroom. A hosted
row may carry `dispatch_only: true`: a label run and the nightly pass over it, and only a
`workflow_dispatch` at a branch runs it, on that branch's head, since it runs the image of
its checkout's own commit, which a merge commit never has and main's head may not have yet.

hosted.why_hosted: A Linux runner with go, git, jj, bun after bun install, awk, python3 and a loopback PostgreSQL server runs this proof. The script builds and starts Dispatch and the daemon itself on databases of its own and starts its own nats-server. It calls the plugin's real daemon client under bun and reaches no outside service.

Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go, git, jj 0.38 or later, awk and python3, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/behind-entry-fence.sh; CI's service satisfies it, and the script starts no container, installing the nats-server it needs with go install

Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go, git, jj 0.38 or later, awk and python3, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/child-adoption.sh; CI's service satisfies it, and this script starts none

Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go, git, jj 0.38 or later, awk and python3, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/conflict-merger.sh; CI's service satisfies it, and the script starts no container, installing the nats-server it needs with go install

Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go, git, jj 0.38 or later, awk and python3, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/conflict-no-takeover.sh; CI's service satisfies it, and the script starts no container, installing the nats-server it needs with go install
DATABASE_URL is required and must name a loopback host; its prerequisite loop takes go, bun, curl, psql and openssl, and it starts no container

Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go, bun, psql and python3, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/dispatch-broker.sh; LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN must name a loopback host, which CI's service satisfies, and the script starts no container. Its default run, K2 and K4, takes a few minutes; LEGION_E2E_TOKEN_RENEWAL=1 runs K3 in about fifteen

Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go, git, jj 0.38 or later, bun (after bun install), awk and python3, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/handoff-records.sh; CI's pgvector service is the server it needs, its role creates Dispatch's database there, it builds and starts Dispatch and the daemon itself, and it reaches no outside service; a run takes two to four minutes

Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go, git, jj 0.38 or later, bun (after bun install), awk and python3, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/owner-steps.sh; CI's pgvector service is the server it needs, its role creates Dispatch's database there, it builds and starts Dispatch and the daemon itself, and it reaches no outside service; a run takes two to five minutes

Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go, git, jj 0.38 or later, bun (after bun install), awk, python3 and tar, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/owner-steps-client.sh; CI's pgvector service is the server it needs, its role creates Dispatch's database there, it builds and starts Dispatch and the daemon itself, and it builds the plugin of the release before from main, which it fetches from origin in a shallow checkout, with a bun install of its own; it reaches no other outside service, and one run on a loaded devbox took fifteen minutes, five of them building that plugin

Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go, git, jj 0.38 or later, awk and python3, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/merge-wait-readable.sh; CI's service satisfies it, and the script starts no container, installing the nats-server it needs with go install

Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go, bun (and bun install), psql, curl, jq and python3, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/nats-callout-sessions.sh; CI's service is the Postgres server dev-stack.sh --callout creates its two databases on, the four sessions (Oh My Pi, Claude Code and two Codex CLI) are this checkout's plugins in processes of their own under stand-in hosts with no model, and the script starts no container. Its --real-hosts mode, the pinned Oh My Pi, Claude Code and Codex CLI on model routes, is run by hand on a Legion pod or a box given the pins and the routes

Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go, awk and python3, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/parent-waits.sh; CI's service is the PostgreSQL it needs, the lib installs the nats-server it needs with go install, and it starts no container and reaches no outside service; a measured run in a pod took 64 seconds, most of it building the driver

Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go, git, jj 0.38 or later, awk and python3, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/phase-entry-converge.sh; the proof needs a real PostgreSQL, which CI's service is, and a real nats-server, which it installs with go install, and it starts no container; a measured run took 45 seconds

Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go, git, jj 0.38 or later, bun (after bun install), awk and python3, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/review-range.sh; CI's pgvector service is the server it needs, its role creates Dispatch's database there, it builds and starts Dispatch and the daemon itself as handoff-records.sh does, and it reaches no outside service; a measured run took 37 seconds with a warm Go build cache

Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go, git, jj 0.38 or later, bun (after bun install), awk and python3, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/plan-ratings.sh; CI's pgvector service is the server it needs, its role creates Dispatch's database there, it builds and starts Dispatch and the daemon itself, and it reaches no outside service; a run takes about a minute with a warm Go build cache and up to five minutes cold

Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go, bun (after bun install), awk and python3, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/register-gate-basis.sh; CI's pgvector service is the server it needs, the rig builds and starts a scratch Dispatch and the daemon itself, the lib installs the nats-server it needs with go install, and it starts no container; a run takes one to five minutes, most of it building the driver and Dispatch

Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go, git, jj 0.38 or later, bun (after bun install), awk and python3, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/experiment.sh; CI's pgvector service is the server it needs, its role creates Dispatch's database there, it builds and starts Dispatch, the daemon and legion itself, and it reaches no outside service; a measured run took about 40 seconds with a warm Go build cache

The daemon refuses to start without tmux on PATH, and CI's tmux is the runner's apt binary; with LEGION_E2E_PG_DSN set the script starts no container of its own, which is how ci.yaml's daemon-go job already runs it

Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go, git, jj 0.38 or later, bun (after bun install), awk and python3, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/step-records.sh; CI's pgvector service is the server it needs, its role creates Dispatch's database there, it builds and starts Dispatch and the daemon itself, and it reaches no outside service; a run takes two to five minutes

Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go, awk and python3, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/sub-architect.sh; CI's service satisfies it, and the script starts no container, installing the nats-server it needs with go install
DATABASE_URL is required and must name a loopback host; its prerequisite loop takes go, bun, curl, psql and openssl, and it starts no container

Run it from a checkout on an amd64 Linux host with docker, go, kubectl, curl, jq, zstd and a tar that supports --zstd, all on a GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 runner, as bash scripts/e2e/shared-clone-kind.sh; it installs kind v0.33.0 by sha256, makes its own kind cluster with gVisor on the node image and busybox .github/ci-images.yaml copies by digest, which a GKE Autopilot cluster cannot (autogke-disallow-privilege refuses its privileged node container), and runs the worker image ghcr.io/cybermonklabs/legion-worker publishes for the checkout's own commit (sha-<12 hex of HEAD>), which needs no secret. It is dispatch_only: worker-image.yaml publishes that image for a pull request's head, and `gh workflow run e2e.yaml --ref <branch> -f script=shared-clone-kind` checks that head out, where a label run checks out the merge commit, for which no image is built, and the nightly main's head, whose image release.yaml builds only for a push whose paths call it, so the nightly cannot rely on the tag existing yet

elsewhere.needs: the pinned Oh My Pi every pane of its part two runs (LEGION_OMP_PATH, an executable, which a GitHub-hosted runner has none of), the model gateway ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL names and a key for it: its key file (APPROVED_VERSION_NEWS_MODEL_KEY_FILE, by default /var/run/model-gateway-key/key), or, where that file holds no key, the pod's own Google identity token for the audience APPROVED_VERSION_NEWS_GATEWAY_AUDIENCE names (the audience the cluster model gateway takes a pod's identity token for), which curl mints from the GKE metadata server in a pod the gateway takes it from, such as a Job of the cluster's builds namespace that carries the deployment's gateway label (<deployment domain>/model-gateway=true), a loopback PostgreSQL with pgvector (LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN), go, git, jj 0.38 or later, tar, awk, python3 and bun with this repository's node_modules, for part two's base arm and for part one's negative control (`--control`) a commit of this repository's own history to take the base from with `git archive` (the parent of the first commit that adds a news mark to the prompts, or, for the control alone, the commit `--base-commit` names), which a shallow CI checkout carries none of, and the wall clock of both parts: part one about two minutes, and the twelve runs of real sessions that part two's driver plans for a full run, each bounded at eight minutes; APPROVED_VERSION_NEWS_STEP, APPROVED_VERSION_NEWS_ARM and APPROVED_VERSION_NEWS_RUNS pick a partial run, a measurement whose last line reads MEASURED, never PASS
a throwaway kind cluster with gVisor on an amd64 Linux host, with docker, go, kubectl, curl, zstd, a tar that supports --zstd and kind, and a worker image by digest (LEGION_E2E_IMAGE)

the pinned Oh My Pi every pane runs (LEGION_OMP_PATH, an absolute executable, which a GitHub-hosted runner has none of), a loopback PostgreSQL (LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN), go, git, jj 0.38 or later, awk, tar, python3 and bun with this repository's node_modules, and, for its negative control, a commit of this repository's own history to take the base tree from with `git archive` (`--base-commit`), which a shallow CI checkout carries none of

a real cluster (LEGION_E2E_RUNTIME_CONTEXT and a worker image by digest), a devbox daemon, a real Claude Code and Oh My Pi on a model route, and the smoke repository
a devbox: tmux, a real Claude Code and Oh My Pi on a model route (LEGION_E2E_MODEL_ROUTE, with a gateway or a key file), and the smoke repository

a Legion pod: tmux, its own model route for both harnesses (LEGION_E2E_MODEL_BASE_URL, LEGION_E2E_MODEL_KEY_FILE, LEGION_E2E_MODEL_ID and LEGION_E2E_CLAUDE_MODEL), the worker image's Oh My Pi and Claude Code pin, and a loopback PostgreSQL (CLEAN_SESSION_STOP_PG_DSN); it starts its own NATS, listener and legion daemon
a devbox: tmux, the pinned Oh My Pi through mise, and its own Postgres and NATS containers, which it fetches from a registry outside this repository's own package (sjawhar/legion#2512)
a throwaway kind cluster with gVisor on an amd64 Linux host, with docker, go, kubectl, curl, zstd, a tar that supports --zstd and kind, and a worker image by digest (LEGION_E2E_IMAGE)

a commit of this repository's own history to build the base from, which it takes with `git archive` from `--base-commit`: a CI checkout is shallow and carries none but its own head, and which commit is `the build before the change` is a caller's choice no job can make. The property the script proves is covered in CI by the Go tests that write an older build's row by raw SQL and assert the drain re-indexes it (`store/refs_grammar_migrations_test.go` and `docs/refs_grammar_drain_test.go`); the script is the live proof of the same thing through two real `envoy-dispatch` binaries, run by hand from a full checkout with go, bun, curl, psql, git, tar, openssl and python3 (which the shared harness runs the loopback guard with) and a loopback PostgreSQL carrying pgvector (DATABASE_URL)

a commit of this repository's own history to build the base from, which it takes with `git archive` from `--base-commit`: a CI checkout is shallow and carries none but its own head, and the commit this proof needs is the release before the five narrowing members, legion-envoy-v29.47.1, which no job can pick for it. It is the live proof that a search carrying one of those members reaches an older build as 404 no route rather than as unnarrowed rows, through two real `envoy-dispatch` binaries, run by hand from a full checkout with go, bun, curl, psql, git, tar, openssl and python3 (which the shared harness runs the loopback guard with) and a loopback PostgreSQL carrying pgvector (DATABASE_URL)

a model provider key of its own for each of its two models, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY, which this repository holds as no secret and will not: Sami answered that no API key goes into cybermonklabs/legion, and that a smoke test which calls a model runs in the deployment repository on workload identity federation (sjawhar/legion#2512)
a devbox: tmux, the pinned Oh My Pi on a model route (LEGION_E2E_MODEL_ROUTE), a Chromium that Playwright drives, and its own Postgres and NATS containers

a pod whose projected Kubernetes credential may create a Job (kubectl -n <namespace> auth can-i create jobs answers yes), the worker image digest to prove (--image, from the Worker Image run's Record digest step) and the deployment's compute class (--node-selector), with the base branch's digest as the negative control (--control); it starts one Job of that image and nothing of its own

the worker image and the Job leak-guard-image-job.sh creates: it is that proof's probe, not a proof of its own, and the harness writes it into the Job's command because a Job holds no checkout to read it from; it runs inside the image against a scratch repository on the Job's emptyDir and judges nothing a runner could give it

the worker image and the Job pack-memory-job.sh creates: it is that measurement's probe, not a proof of its own, and the harness writes it and lib/pack-memory-peak.py into the Job's command because a Job holds no checkout to read them from; it runs the image's own cache, fetch and provision on the Job's disk volume and judges nothing a runner could give it

a pod whose projected Kubernetes credential may create a Job (kubectl -n <namespace> auth can-i create jobs answers yes), kubectl, jq and a checkout of the head measured, whose double of Cloud Storage it writes into the Job's command, the worker image digest to test (--image, from the Worker Image run's Record digest step), and the deployment's compute class, storage class, labels and annotations (--node-selector, --storage-class, --label, --annotation, or --job-settings); it starts one gVisor Job of that image with a disk volume of 120Gi and 16 CPU for its fetchers by default, about ten minutes on the default repository (nodejs/node), and nothing of its own

the worker image and the Job repository-cache-burst-job.sh creates: it is that measurement's probe, not a proof of its own, and the harness writes it and the double's sources into the Job's command because a Job holds no checkout to read them from; it runs the image's own cache and provision against that double in three containers of one pod and judges nothing a runner could give it, bar its self-test, which runs on any Linux host with bash 4 or later, GNU coreutils, jq and awk
a live multi-repository run on the production cluster: it is the operator's acceptance observer, reads that run's daemon, Dispatch, GitHub and kubectl, and starts nothing of its own

a deployed Dispatch and the operator's own credential: the dispatch command on PATH, run in the operator's own shell with its session (DISPATCH_HOST and DISPATCH_SESSION_ID) and the deployed Dispatch and token its envoy.json or DISPATCH_URL and DISPATCH_TOKEN name, a project key, and the key of one issue of that project a deployed Legion ran to done after the release that rates each plan; it reads the project's finished issues and starts nothing, and needs no checkout of this repository, only lib/dispatch-read.sh beside it
